title: The trouble store folds what is pending before it answers a read
intention: cairn/devices/trouble: every read of the held store (TroubleDevice.live, all, get/show and the shim's read verbs) first folds every pending emission, serialized by an exclusive flock on the watermark file so two readers never fold twice; and a raise emission whose detail is not a mapping folds as {'note': <the value>} instead of refusing, so a legacy emission cannot wedge its source's lane.
why: Akien 2026-10-10: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", pre-approved through PROVED. This ticket closes live trouble /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/troubles/trouble-drain-has-no-host-the-beat-backstop-is-prose.json, a measured fault that enters as a bug (skills/intent/SKILL.md: a bug enters as a ticket, not through /intent). Re-measured 2026-10-10 by cc0: the ground loop pulses nothing by design (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/__main__.py: 'No bus, no probes, no shims ... no pulse calls', ticket bae622881f03), so TroubleShim.on_pulse never runs; systemctl --user lists cairn-bus, cairn-ground-loop, cairn-web-server and no trouble host. A hand TroubleShim().drain() folded 7 pending emissions and refused 1: harbor_master/0/20261009.000059.516741 (string detail), which per _fold's own docstring wedges that source's watermark.
traces_to: Law 4 (the backstop is physics, not a docstring); Law 7 (a fault raised is a fault the reader sees); memory a-provider-doesnt-know-its-consumers (the consumer asks).
how: cairn/devices/trouble only. (1) Move the drain body so the device can call it: a module-level fold_pending(root, roots) in the trouble package (shim.drain delegates to it), holding fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) on the watermark file for the whole fold. (2) TroubleDevice.live(), all() and the get/show read path call fold_pending first; a fold that raises is caught, recorded on the returned value's side channel / stderr, and the read still answers (a read never fails because a fold did). (3) _fold for the raise gate: detail = values.get('detail'); if not a dict and not None -> {'note': detail}. (4) on_pulse and receive_raise stay. Docstrings that say 'the beat drains it' are corrected to 'the next read drains it'.
falsifier: cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_a_read_folds_what_is_pending.py under PROVES {'3c62020b0d88': {'1','2','3'}} on a scratch roots tree: (1) an emission written to a fixture source's log dir is not in the store's file until TroubleDevice(...).live() is called, and is in live()'s answer; (2) a raise emission with a string detail folds as {'note': ...} and a later emission from the same source folds too (the lane is not wedged); (3) two processes calling live() at once over 20 pending emissions leave every count exactly 1. Hollow: removing the fold from live() reds 1. In the verdict, the live pending count after one `cairn trouble list` is 0.

decisions.text: The read is the event that drains, not a daemon and not the beat: Akien ruled the ground loop is only a heartbeat (bae622881f03) and probes/mail fire on their events; a reader is the consumer asking. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
A legacy non-mapping detail folds as {'note': value}; the raise door refusing it going forward is ticket 906ceb765d0a. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The non-mapping detail rule is already built and PROVED by 114002d08c46: _fold carries a string detail as {'text': s} and any other non-dict as {'text': json.dumps(v)}. This ticket does not touch it; D2's {'note': ...} shape is read as {'text': ...}, and the proof's tooth 2 asserts the occurrence's 'text' is the string. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

shim.py gains module-level fold_pending(device, roots=None): it builds TroubleShim(roots=roots, root=device._root), sets shim._device = device (the reading device is handed in, so a read never starts or registers a second device), and runs the walk under _fold_lock. The drain body stays in the shim as _drain_walk, which first sets _watermarks = None so the watermark is re-read inside the lock; drain() takes the same lock BEFORE _ensure_device, because starting the device reads introspect() -> live(), which would otherwise fold first and leave drain reporting nothing. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

_fold_lock(path) is a contextmanager: fcntl.flock LOCK_EX on drained.json.lock beside drained.json (never on the watermark itself: opening it to lock would create it empty, and an empty watermark reads as unreadable and refuses every later drain), and a threading.local set of held lock paths: a fold inside a fold in the same thread yields False and returns {'outcome': 'reentrant', 'folded': []} instead of waiting on itself. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

TroubleDevice.__init__(root=None, *, roots=None). A read folds only when root is None (the live store folds the live log homes) or roots is given (a scratch store folds the homes its caller names); a scratch root with no roots folds nothing, so it can never advance the live watermark. TroubleShim._start_device passes roots. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The fold hook is TroubleDevice.fold_pending(), called first in all(); live() and state() read through all(). There is no public get/show on TroubleDevice (measured: grep 'def get|def show' in cairn/devices/trouble is empty), and `cairn trouble get status` answers from the shim's cached last_known, so all() is the whole read path. A fold that raises prints 'trouble: fold before read failed: <type>: <text>' to stderr and the read answers from the store as it stands. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

_drain_walk lists each source directory once with os.listdir and splits names by the '.<gate>.json' suffix, keeping only names above that gate's watermark. Measured 2026-10-11: three globs per source cost 1.2 s per read over ~280,000 log files; one listing costs 0.2 s with nothing pending. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The falsifier's verdict clause reads 'after one read': `cairn trouble list` lists the device's verbs and reads no trouble (measured 2026-10-11), so the verdict instrument calls TroubleDevice().live() once and then counts emissions above their gate's watermark across every source; exit 0 means pending 0. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Wording: shim.py's receive_raise docstring says the ticket exists now, 'not when someone next asks' (was 'not on the next pulse'); the header gains a paragraph 'THE READ IS THE EVENT THAT DRAINS'; the charter's DELIVERY edge says 'the next read folds it' through `cairn artifact write`, with recompile_gate.sh poked at commit. on_pulse and receive_raise stay. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The lock file is <watermark dir>/drained.json.lock, where the watermark dir is the directory holding TroubleShim's existing drained.json (shim._watermark_path().parent, WATERMARK_NAME, both unchanged by this build); the re-entrancy guard is one module-level threading.local whose 'held' attribute is a set of lock paths. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Emission filenames begin with a fixed-width UTC stamp (YYYYMMDD.HHMMSS.micro), so 'above the watermark' is plain string comparison name > watermark, exactly the comparison the existing drain already uses; only the enumeration changes (one os.listdir per source instead of one glob per gate). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The proof is cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_a_read_folds_what_is_pending.py, in the same plain-python tooth format as test_a_text_detail_still_lands.py, with three teeth: a_read_folds_what_is_pending (a pending raise in scratch roots folds on TroubleDevice(root, roots=...).live()), a_text_detail_does_not_wedge_the_read (a string-detail raise folds with occurrence text == the string and a later raise from the same source also folds), two_readers_fold_each_emission_once (two forked readers over 20 pending leave every count 1). It is written red first, before the read-path change. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
